hook: Paul Viola was born in New York City on October 22, 1966, and studied at MIT, earning a PhD in 1995 with a thesis on alignment by maximization of mutual information under advisors Christopher Atkeson and Tomas Lozano-Perez. He went on to work at MIT, the Cambridge Research Laboratory of Compaq and Hewlett Packard, and Mitsubishi Electric Research Laboratories before joining Microsoft Research. In 2001, with Michael Jones, he published Rapid Object Detection using a Boosted Cascade of Simple Features, which combined Haar like features, an integral image representation and a cascade of boosted classifiers to detect faces in video in real time. The Viola-Jones framework became the standard method for real time face detection for more than a decade and was built into consumer cameras and photo software. Viola later held research and engineering leadership roles at Microsoft, Amazon Prime Air and the self driving vehicle company Zoox, continuing to work on computer vision and machine learning problems.
